citations.claim: Body 1 sits exactly on its waypoint with ~zero velocity just before failure
Next step body 1 position/velocity became non-finite (NaN)

counterfactual.change: Moved waypoint x by +0.5 (8.0176->8.5176) so body never sits exactly at zero distance to waypoint; otherwise identical. Failure disappears.

explanation: Controlled body 1 converges exactly onto its waypoint (position equals waypoint, speed ~1e-15 at step 1951). On the next step its state becomes NaN. Likely cause: the velocity-error/waypoint steering law normalizes the to-waypoint vector (dividing by distance) without a zero-distance guard, so exact arrival yields 0/0 = NaN which propagates into commanded force/velocity and then position.
vision_note: Through steps 1949 to 1951 bodies rest near the floor and move normally with no visible anomaly. At step 1952 the small red body disappears near the green waypoint cross and all subsequent tiles are blank black, indicating the state became invalid and unrenderable.
